title: Check yourself: The model family and choosing a tier

questions.stem: A team tags 50,000 short support tickets overnight, each with one of eight categories. Speed per ticket is irrelevant, spend matters, and the categories are easy to tell apart. What is the best first step?

options.text: Begin with the lowest-priced tier and score it on genuine samples
options.says: Simple, high-volume, cost-sensitive work fits the efficiency-first path, validated on real data (the two strategies).

options.text: Begin with Claude Opus 5.5, because the overview names it the usual starting point
options.says: Ruled out because the efficiency-first path says to "Begin with the fast, low-cost tier, test thoroughly, and move up only for a gap you can name", and the overview's default is only a starting point for most workloads.

options.text: Begin with the top tier, then step down if the budget complains
options.says: Ruled out because the capability-first path is "Suited to complex reasoning, accuracy that outweighs cost, and high-autonomy agent work", and this task is the opposite.

options.text: Send the first thousand to each tier and keep whichever answers quickest
options.says: Ruled out because the decision rule is to "compare accuracy, quality and edge-case handling", and speed per ticket is irrelevant here.

origin.section: How the documentation says to choose

questions.stem: A coding agent running on the mid tier fails a handful of hard tasks each day. The team plans to move the entire system to the top tier. Which alternative should they try first?

options.text: Move all traffic to Claude Fable 5.1, then work the effort down later
options.says: Ruled out because the largest model "raises cost and latency on work that does not need it", and effort would do.

options.text: Drop to the fastest tier and retry each failure several times
options.says: Ruled out because the efficiency-first path says to "move up only for a gap you can name", and retrying hard tasks on a weaker tier moves the wrong way.

options.text: Run the difficult cases at higher effort and measure the change
options.says: The page says tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models, and a narrower change targets the hard tasks only.

options.text: Pin the id to a dated snapshot so results stop varying
options.says: Ruled out because "an id with a retirement date needs a migration plan before the date, not after" is about the life of an id and says nothing about capability.
